purpose: Teach: 洗剤/ひとまず/ナイス/プチ/デカ/ポチ/ダッシュ/バッチリ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の洗剤、香り、強かったな。
lines.en: Old detergent had such a strong scent, didn't it…
lines.style: Gentle, distant gaze into memory. Soft opening. Slow, measured pace like watching a faded photograph. Trailing off as if the scent is still somehow present.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。今日は、ひとまず、お茶でも飲みましょう。
lines.en: Yes. For now, shall we have some tea?
lines.style: Warm and settling, like pouring tea itself. Steady, easy cadence. A small gesture that says 'I'm here, let's take our time.' Soft close on the question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の野球、ナイスなホームラン、覚えてる?
lines.en: Do you remember? That nice home run when we were young, playing baseball…
lines.style: Quiet, turning inward. Lifting slightly on the memory itself — the home run gets a small lift of pride. Then settling back into reflection. Not seeking confirmation, just speaking aloud to share the moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 孫の手土産、プチケーキ、可愛かったわ。
lines.en: The souvenir the grandchild brought — that little cake was so sweet, wasn't it.
lines.style: Gentle warmth in the voice, like holding something delicate. Soft attack. Lingering fondly on 'little cake.' Smile underneath the words, not performed but genuinely there.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔のスーパー、駅前、デカい建物だった。
lines.en: That old supermarket by the station — such a big building it was…
lines.style: Slow, gazing backward. Weight and substance on 'big building' — it looms in memory. Breathing is easy, unhurried. Trailing off into the image of it.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 近所のポチ、毎朝、散歩で会うね。
lines.en: You know, we run into the neighbor's Pochi every morning on our walk.
lines.style: Quiet observation, like noticing something small that matters. Steady, present-tense comfort. A small smile lives in this one. Not performing gentleness, just being present with the fact of it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、運動会で、ダッシュ、得意だった。
lines.en: Back when I was young, I was quite quick on sports day — loved the dash.
lines.style: A small flicker of pride on 'quite quick.' Otherwise measured and reflective. Not boasting, just remembering what his body could do. Pace slows slightly at the end, settling into the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 夕食の準備、もう、バッチリ整ったわよ。
lines.en: Dinner's all ready — I've got everything set for us.
lines.style: Bright, accomplished ease. Quick, competent rhythm. A small note of satisfaction that things are in order. Warm close that settles like a contented sigh — 'we're taken care of.'
